analysis.title: Under Armour Inc. (UAA): F2Q27 First Take: Better North America trends and well-controlled SG&A; FY EPS guide reaffirmed
key_insights: UAA F2Q27 adjusted EPS (comparable, recurring) was $0.00 versus GS/FactSet consensus of -$0.01, a slight beat. Net revenues were $1.242bn, down 6.9% Y/Y (-7.3% ex-FX), versus GS/consensus of -8.7%/-7.9%.

Gross margin contracted about 30bps Y/Y to 47.0%, below GS/consensus of 47.3%/47.5%, on unfavorable FX, channel and regional mix, and pricing, partly offset by supply-chain benefits and favorable product mix.
Adjusted SG&A fell 3% to $559mn, or 45.0% of sales, versus GS/consensus of 46.0%/45.9%. Adjusted EBIT margin was 2.0% versus GS/consensus of 1.3%/1.1%.
FY27 adjusted EPS guidance was reaffirmed at $0.08-$0.12 (GS/consensus $0.10/$0.11). Revenue is still expected to decline mid-single digits and adjusted SG&A to decline low-single digits.

FY27 gross margin outlook was lowered to +170-220bps Y/Y from +220-270bps, about 50bps at the midpoint. The reasons given are higher fuel and freight costs, planned inventory management actions, and FX headwinds.

Adjusted EBIT guidance was maintained at $140-$160mn (GS/consensus $145.9mn/$143.5mn). It includes about $70mn of benefit from prior-year IEEPA tariff refunds. Middle East-related headwinds rose to about $45mn from $35mn.
Inventories rose 4.0% Y/Y to $1.076bn, versus a GS expectation of a 4.0% Y/Y decline. Management cited planned inventory actions in the updated outlook.

By region, North America declined 6.9% Y/Y (-6.6% ex-FX) versus GS/consensus of -8.5%/-11.1%. EMEA fell 8.5% (-8.0% ex-FX) versus -11.7%/-12.0%. APAC fell 8.8% (-11.6% ex-FX) versus -8.2%/-6.7%. LatAm grew 3.0% (-3.5% ex-FX) versus +6.7%/+1.0%.
Wholesale decreased 6.5% and DTC declined 8.2%, including a 7% decline in owned-and-operated stores and a 12% decline in eCommerce.
GS is Neutral on UAA with a $5.50 12-month price target based on 9.75x Q5-Q8 EV/EBITDA. The stock closed at $5.57 on 5 Nov 2026, implying 1.3% downside.

market_movers.rationale: Revenue and adjusted EBIT beat expectations on lower SG&A, but gross margin missed and the FY27 gross margin guide was cut by about 50bps. Inventory is up 4% Y/Y.

earnings_insights: F2Q27 reported 11/6 (first take): adjusted/comparable recurring EPS $0.00 versus GS/FactSet consensus est -$0.01. GAAP EPS was $0.00 versus GS est $0.02, and F2Q26 GAAP EPS was -$0.04.
F2Q27 reported net revenue $1.242bn (-6.9% Y/Y) versus GS est $1.218bn (-8.7%). Reported adjusted EBIT margin was 2.0% versus GS est 1.3% and consensus 1.1%.
FY27 guidance reaffirmed: adjusted EPS $0.08-$0.12 versus GS est $0.10 and consensus $0.11. Adjusted EBIT guidance of $140-$160mn compares with GS est $145.9mn and consensus $143.5mn.
GS expects the call to cover F2H revenue cadence, North America and APAC trends, gross margin puts and takes, the timing of inventory actions, and the macro and consumer backdrop.
risk_factors: Upside: stronger brand and product traction, DTC reacceleration supporting structural margin expansion, faster recovery in international markets.

Downside: prolonged North America weakness, margin recovery stalling amid promotional and cost pressure, competitive intensity limiting share recovery, a tougher macro backdrop weighing on discretionary demand.
Inventory up 4% Y/Y with planned inventory management actions ahead.
FY27 EBIT guidance includes about $70mn from IEEPA tariff refunds.
geopolitical: Middle East-related headwinds to UAA increased to about $45mn from $35mn in the prior outlook.
